original_test_intent: During a controlled repeated SUT power transition, verify that the BMC Redfish Systems endpoint returns the project's expected HTTP 503 Service Unavailable response in the defined transient phase, then returns normal service after readiness, without mislabeling connection loss, TLS/authentication failure or ordinary host-off inventory as 503.
original_method: Select the unique row; identify SUT/BMC/PDU/IPMI power path and firmware; define cycle type/count/off/on/dwell/readiness/final state and exact phase expected to yield 503; drain workloads and establish console/recovery; capture a TLS-validated 2xx baseline with full status/headers/body; synchronize a monotonic cycle controller with bounded Redfish polling; for every attempt record DNS/TCP/TLS/HTTP timing, status and body plus BMC/host power/readiness; abort on faults; verify at least/each required 503 only in the approved phase and 2xx recovery afterward; preserve all logs and final health without hardcoded secrets.
manual_activity: An operator approves/quiesces the DUT and controls or supervises the exact power-cycle sequence and recovery; the agent may run bounded TLS-valid Redfish polling and correlate responses to supplied phase markers.
required_inputs: SUT/BMC/firmware plus PSU/feed/PDU/IPMI controller and power-domain mapping
Definition of power cycle: host soft/off-on, DC, AC or another boundary; count, intervals, dwell, stabilization and final state
Exact BMC/host phase and time window where `/Systems` must return 503, expected response headers/body and per-cycle/aggregate acceptance
Protected TLS/authentication, poll cadence/timeouts, boot/BMC readiness oracles, workload drain, aborts and independent console/recovery
safety_requirements: Use a dedicated drained SUT and prove correct power-controller mapping before cycling
Require explicit authorization for the exact count/timing and never infer AC/DC/host cycle semantics
Protect credentials and validate endpoint certificate/identity
Distinguish DNS/TCP/TLS/auth timeouts from an actual received HTTP 503 and retain full response metadata
Abort on boot/BMC/power/thermal/storage fault or missed readiness; do not automatically repeat a failed cycle
agent_execution_scope: Perform read-only baseline and synchronized bounded HTTP polling
After approved operator/controller power actions, classify each attempt by cycle phase and network/TLS/HTTP outcome
Verify normal service and target health after every cycle and at final state
Do not choose/issue unapproved power actions, expose secrets, convert connection failures to 503, retry abnormal cycles or decide verdict
engineer_actions: Approve cycle boundary, controller, count, timing, readiness and final state
Approve why/when a BMC Redfish 503 is expected during SUT power transition and exact headers/body/occurrence rule
Approve polling/timeouts, workload drain, aborts and console/power recovery
Review phase/status timeline and decide PASS, FAIL, or BLOCKED

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: Repeated GETs are appropriate observation, but generic `ipmitool chassis power off/on` is an unapproved interpretation of 'power cycle stress'; host off commonly leaves BMC reachable, so 503 needs a defined transition rather than assumption.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: Use TLS-validated protected GETs with explicit connect/total timeouts and full status/header/body capture while an approved controller supplies phase markers; power commands are separately authorized and not invented by this review.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: Continuous Systems GET during power-cycle stress, literal 503 criterion and 60/60-minute estimate remain; cycle count/interval and controller are pending.

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Capture a phase-locked timeline that separates physical/host power state, BMC readiness and DNS/TCP/TLS/HTTP outcomes, requiring genuine server-originated 503 evidence and post-cycle 2xx recovery for every approved cycle.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Adds power-domain definition, exact cycle/readiness contract, layered network classification, full response oracle, per-cycle health and stop/recovery rules.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: A curl failure or zero code is not 503, while `/Systems` may legitimately return 200 and `PowerState=Off` when only the host is off; a 503 must be tied to the specified BMC transition.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: Repeated cycling stresses power, storage and firmware startup paths and can leave the host or BMC unavailable; overly rapid polling can itself load a recovering BMC and distort results.

project_override_considerations: If vendor design says host-off `/Systems` remains 2xx and no BMC service transition should occur, engineering must correct the Review-layer 503 phase or identify the intended cycle (for example BMC restart/AC restoration) while preserving Master. No connection failure may be counted as the literal HTTP criterion.
expected_evidence: Workload drain, console and recovery readiness
Baseline TLS-valid 2xx request plus endpoint/client metadata
Per-attempt monotonic timestamp, cycle/phase marker and DNS/TCP/TLS/HTTP classification with redacted status/headers/body/error
Per-cycle genuine 503 occurrence according to oracle and post-readiness 2xx/System power-state recovery
SEL/host/boot/power logs, abort/recovery/final health and engineer verdict

engineering_decision_pending.question: Resolve Functionality row 2251 Wistron-BMC Sanity-00033-V001: approve the SUT/BMC/firmware and exact power boundary/controller (host, DC, AC or other), cycle count, off/on/dwell/stabilization/readiness/final state; define the precise phase/time window and server-originated headers/body where `/redfish/v1/Systems` must return HTTP 503 versus expected 2xx/PowerState Off or network/TLS failure, occurrence rule and polling limits; approve workload drain, aborts and independent console/power recovery.

review_improvement: Preserves the literal 503-under-cycle coverage while preventing unsafe undefined cycling or a transport outage from masquerading as the required HTTPS response.
independent_technical_reasoning: HTTP 503 is an application-layer response, so the BMC must accept the connection and deliberately report temporary unavailability. Removing host power alone often does not remove BMC standby power; Redfish can remain healthy and report the host off. Conversely, AC removal may eliminate networking entirely, yielding no HTTP response. Therefore acceptance depends on an explicitly documented transition phase and a layer-by-layer timeline. The polling is automatable, but the repeated power action and recovery cannot proceed without a bounded human-approved plan.
